title: Physiological and training characteristics of recreational marathon runners
authors: Gordon D, Wightman S, Basevitch I, Johnstone J, Espejo-Sanchez C, Beckford C, et al.
journal: Open Access Journal of Sports Medicine
population: 97 recreational marathon runners (63 male, 34 female; age 42.4 +/- 9.9 y; marathon time 229.1 +/- 48.7 min)
findings: Runners were grouped by finish time (2.5-3, 3-3.5, 3.5-4, 4-4.5 and >4.5 h) and completed treadmill tests (LT1, LT2, economy, VO2max) plus a training questionnaire.
Training frequency was greater in the 2.5-3 h group than the 3.5-4 h (P<0.001) and >4.5 h groups (P=0.004).
Race speed correlated with LT1 (r=0.791), LT2 (r=0.721) and distance per session (r=0.563); discriminating training variables were frequency and absolute training speed.
limitations: Small convenience sample, self-reported training, unadjusted for age and sex, no weekly volume per band in the abstract. The reported P values for 2.5-3 h vs 3.5-4 h distance (16.1 vs 15.5 km, P=0.01) look odd and should be checked in the full text.
implications: Use session length and frequency as bands that rise with goal time: about 16 km per session near 3 h, about 15 km sub-4 h, about 10 km for finishers over 4.5 h.
Link training speed to lactate-threshold zones; estimate thresholds from heart-rate and pace data when no lab test exists.
